name: Proofpoint
desc: Provides email security, data loss prevention and security awareness software to enterprises and government organisations worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.050bn in 2020 (Wikipedia infobox); taken private by Thoma Bravo for USD 12.3bn in 2021
markets: Enterprises worldwide; acquired Germany's Hornetsecurity (May 2025) and agreed to buy Varonis (Oct 2026)
rationale: Acquisitive security platform building a global enterprise brand; rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta already use F1 for CIO hospitality.

name: McAfee
desc: Sells consumer antivirus, identity protection and online privacy software, often bundled with PCs and telecom plans.
ownership: private equity: Advent International and Permira
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.92bn in 2021 (Wikipedia infobox); taken private by an Advent-led group in 2022
markets: Consumers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through retail, PC makers and telecom partners
rationale: Mass-market consumer security brand needing global awareness; Bitdefender and 1Password show F1 works for consumer security.

name: Veeam
desc: Develops backup, disaster recovery and ransomware resilience software for enterprise data across cloud, virtual and physical systems.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1bn in 2019 (Wikipedia infobox); annual recurring revenue above USD 1.5bn reported in March 2024
markets: Enterprises worldwide with regional headquarters in Paris, Columbus, Dubai and Sydney
rationale: Global B2B data-resilience brand competing with Rubrik and Cohesity; Rubrik already uses F1 to reach enterprise IT buyers.

name: Trellix
desc: Provides extended detection and response, endpoint and network security, formed from McAfee Enterprise and FireEye products.
capacity_detail: About USD 2bn annual revenue at launch in January 2022 (Wikipedia)
markets: More than 40,000 enterprise and government customers worldwide
rationale: Large enterprise security vendor needing brand visibility after merger; competitors CrowdStrike and Zscaler are active F1 partners.

name: Optiv
desc: Provides cybersecurity consulting, systems integration and managed security services to large enterprises and public bodies.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.5bn in 2018 (Wikipedia)
markets: Mainly large enterprises and public-sector clients in the United States and Canada
rationale: Services firm selling to CISOs; F1 hospitality could support enterprise relationship selling alongside its vendor partners.

name: Entrust
industry: digital identity and payment card security
desc: Provides digital certificates, identity verification, card issuance and encryption products to banks, governments and enterprises.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 916.7M in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox); owned by the Quandt family investment office since 1987
markets: Banks, governments and enterprises worldwide, including passport and border programmes
rationale: Quandt-owned trust brand selling to banks and governments globally; F1 hospitality suits long enterprise and public-sector sales cycles.

name: ESET
desc: Develops antivirus, endpoint protection and threat intelligence software for consumers and businesses, sold worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 733M in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Consumers and businesses worldwide, with 11 research and development centres
rationale: European consumer and SME security brand competing with Bitdefender, which already sponsors F1; global awareness drives retail sales.

name: Kaspersky
desc: Develops antivirus, endpoint security and threat intelligence products for consumers and businesses outside the United States.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 836M in 2025 (Wikipedia finances table)
sponsorships: Former Scuderia Ferrari partner; deal paused March 2022
markets: Consumers and businesses in Russia, Asia, Middle East, Africa and Latin America; banned from selling in the US
rationale: Former Ferrari partner with F1 history, but US sanctions and the paused 2022 deal make a return very difficult.

name: Zerodha
desc: Runs India's discount stockbroking and trading app Kite, offering equities, derivatives and mutual fund investing.
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 8,847 crore (USD 950M) in FY25 (Wikipedia)
markets: Retail investors and traders across India
rationale: Highly profitable founder-owned broker; F1's fast-growing Indian audience could build brand against Groww and Angel One.

name: Trading 212
desc: Offers a commission-free investing app for shares, ETFs and CFDs to retail clients across Europe and beyond.
capacity_detail: Trading 212 UK Limited revenue GBP 277.6M in 2025 (Wikipedia)
markets: Retail investors across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America and Asia-Pacific; regulated in UK, Germany, Cyprus, Australia
rationale: Pan-European trading app competing with eToro and Revolut, both F1 partners; F1 fanbase matches its young retail investor target.

name: Tether
desc: Issues USDT, the largest US-dollar stablecoin, used for crypto trading, payments and remittances worldwide.
capacity_detail: Record profit of USD 13bn in 2024 (revenue therefore higher); about USD 10bn profit in 2025 (Wikipedia)
sponsorships: Minority shareholder in Juventus (from Feb 2025); USD 1.29bn bid for Juventus rejected Dec 2025
markets: Crypto traders and users of dollar payments worldwide, especially emerging markets in Latin America, Africa and Asia
rationale: Hugely profitable stablecoin issuer investing in sport; rivals Circle and crypto platforms already use F1 for global brand legitimacy.

name: BharatPe
desc: Provides QR-code payments, point-of-sale terminals and loans to small merchants and shopkeepers across India.
capacity_detail: Series E USD 370M at USD 2.85bn valuation (Aug 2021), per cited Financial Express headline
markets: Small merchants and grocery stores across India
rationale: Domestic merchant brand; F1 relevance limited to India's growing audience, so a regional race or digital deal at most.

name: MoneyGram
desc: Provides international money transfers through agent locations and digital apps in more than 200 countries and territories.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 900M in 2019 (Wikipedia infobox); taken private by Madison Dearborn for USD 1bn, closed June 2023
sponsorships: Title sponsor of MoneyGram Haas F1 Team 2023-2025; replaced by Toyota Gazoo Racing for 2026
markets: Senders and receivers in more than 200 countries and territories through about 400,000 agent locations
rationale: Lapsed Haas title sponsor with proven F1 activation playbook; could return as a smaller team or race partner to defend global brand.

name: Travelex
desc: Sells foreign currency, travel money cards and international payments through airport stores, ATMs and online.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 553.3M in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox); owned by its former debt holders since 2020 restructuring
sponsorships: Former sponsor of Panasonic Toyota Racing F1 team (2002-2003) and Australia men's cricket team (2001-2010)
markets: Travellers in over 20 countries via 600-plus stores and 700-plus ATMs, mainly airports
rationale: Former F1 team sponsor whose travelling, internationally mobile customers overlap with F1's race-going and airport audience.

name: Infoblox
desc: Provides DNS, DHCP and IP address management software with DNS-based threat detection for enterprise networks.
ownership: private equity: Vista Equity Partners and Warburg Pincus
capacity_detail: Over USD 400M annual recurring revenue in 2023, per PitchBook as cited by Wikipedia
markets: Enterprises and service providers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Enterprise networking-security vendor; F1 hospitality could support CIO selling, as Cisco, Extreme Networks and Zscaler already do.

name: WeLab
desc: Runs WeLab Bank, a Hong Kong virtual bank, plus digital lending and banking businesses in mainland China and Indonesia.
capacity_detail: Total funding over USD 580M after Series C in late 2019 (Wikipedia)
markets: Hong Kong, mainland China and Indonesia (Bank Jasa Jakarta, Maucash)
rationale: Asian digital bank seeking brand recognition against incumbents; Singapore and Shanghai races offer regional activation.

name: Aikido Security
desc: Provides an all-in-one application and cloud security platform that finds and fixes code vulnerabilities for developers.
capacity_detail: USD 60M Series B at a USD 1bn valuation on 14 January 2026 (Wikipedia)
markets: Software teams in Europe and North America, with offices in Ghent, San Francisco, London and Chicago

signals.raise: USD 60M Series B at USD 1bn valuation (Jan 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aikido_Security)

rationale: Fast-growing European security unicorn targeting developers; F1's tech-savvy audience and Belgian Grand Prix heritage suit brand building.

name: Torq
desc: Provides an AI-driven security operations platform that automates alert triage, investigation and response for security teams.
capacity_detail: Total raised USD 330M, latest USD 140M Series D in January 2026 (New Market Pitch funding tracker)
markets: Enterprise security teams, mainly in North America, Europe and Israel
rationale: Well-funded Israeli-founded SOC automation vendor competing with CrowdStrike, an F1 partner; hospitality could accelerate enterprise deals.

name: Sentra
desc: Provides cloud data security software that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data across cloud and AI environments.
capacity_detail: Total raised USD 253M, latest USD 150M Series C in November 2026 (New Market Pitch funding tracker)
markets: Enterprises in North America, Europe and Israel

signals.raise: USD 150M Series C led by Capital One Ventures (Nov 2026; https://www.bankingnewsai.com/fintech/neobanks/fintech-funding-2026)

rationale: Freshly funded data-security challenger to Cyera; an F1 team deal could build enterprise brand awareness quickly.

name: Invicti Security
desc: Provides dynamic application security testing tools, including Acunetix and Netsparker, that scan web applications for vulnerabilities.
capacity_detail: Total raised USD 665M, including USD 625M growth equity in October 2021 (New Market Pitch funding tracker)
markets: Enterprises and government bodies in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific
rationale: PE-backed application security vendor; F1 hospitality could support enterprise selling against larger rivals with motorsport deals.

name: CertiK
desc: Audits smart contracts and blockchain projects, and monitors Web3 security risks through its Skynet platform.
capacity_detail: Total raised USD 289M+, latest USD 60M Series B3 extension in April 2022 (New Market Pitch funding tracker)
markets: Blockchain projects, exchanges and crypto firms worldwide, especially Asia and North America
rationale: Web3 security brand serving crypto firms that already sponsor F1 heavily; motorsport exposure reaches the same crypto audience.

name: Fasset
desc: Runs an AI-powered stablecoin neobanking app for moving, holding and spending money across currencies and asset classes.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 1bn after USD 68M Series C (2026), per Fintech News UAE
markets: Cross-border users moving, holding and spending money across currencies, mainly in the Gulf region

signals.raise: USD 68M Series C led by SBI Group at USD 1bn valuation (2026; https://fintechnews.ae/33455/funding/the-middle-easts-9-fintech-unicorns-as-of-september-2026/)

rationale: Dubai stablecoin neobank with Asian and Gulf users; Abu Dhabi, Bahrain and Saudi races offer home-region activation like crypto rivals.

name: Hargreaves Lansdown
desc: Runs the UK's largest retail investment platform, offering share dealing, funds, ISAs and pensions online and by app.
ownership: private equity: CVC Capital Partners, Nordic Capital and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority
capacity_detail: Taken private at a GBP 5.4bn valuation (agreed Aug 2024, delisted March 2025); revenue GBP 764.9M in 2024
markets: About 1.9 million UK retail investors with GBP 155bn of assets (Aug 2024)
rationale: New PE owners investing to defend share against Trading 212 and Revolut; British Grand Prix and UK F1 fanbase match its affluent investors.

name: Black Duck
desc: Provides software composition analysis and application security testing tools that find vulnerabilities and licence risks in code.
ownership: private equity: Clearlake Capital Group and Francisco Partners
capacity_detail: Bought from Synopsys for USD 2.1bn in 2024 by Clearlake and Francisco Partners (Wikipedia)
markets: Enterprise software developers worldwide; about 2,000 employees in 2024
rationale: Newly independent security brand rebuilding identity after carve-out; F1 B2B hospitality could reach enterprise engineering leaders.

name: IDEMIA
desc: Provides biometric identification, secure payment cards and digital identity technology to governments, banks and telecom operators.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.9bn in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Governments, banks and mobile operators worldwide; about 15,000 employees
rationale: Global identity-security supplier to banks and governments; F1 hospitality suits large public-sector and banking deals, though brand is B2B.

name: Bitstack
desc: French fintech app that lets customers save small amounts in bitcoin through round-ups and recurring purchases.
capacity_detail: Sleeve sponsor on RC Lens home and away kits for 2026-27 UEFA Champions League matches (announced 19 Aug 2026)
sponsorships: RC Lens Champions League sleeve sponsor 2026-27
markets: Retail savers mainly in France
rationale: Young bitcoin savings app already buying top-tier football; F1 digital or French GP-linked activation could follow, but budget likely small.

name: Aircash
desc: Croatian e-money app for cash deposits, payments, money transfers and a linked Aircash Mastercard, licensed across the EU.
capacity_detail: Main shirt sponsor of Serie A club Hellas Verona in 2025-26 (Wikipedia season kits table)
markets: Croatia, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina and other EU markets; 1.9 million users (company site)
rationale: Expanding EU e-money app already paying for a Serie A shirt; F1 regional digital or race-level deals could extend its awareness push.

name: B2BinPAY
desc: Provides a crypto payment gateway, crypto-to-fiat payouts, token swaps and wallets for merchants and businesses.
capacity_detail: Sleeve sponsor of La Liga club Athletic Bilbao in 2025-26 (Wikipedia season kits table; company site says official Athletic sponsor)
markets: Merchants in most countries except the US, Canada, Russia and Iran; entities in El Salvador and Mauritius
rationale: Crypto payments firm already buying La Liga exposure; crypto rivals use F1 heavily, so a team-level partnership is plausible.
